# Executive Summary

This document defines the architecture and integration roadmap for expanding `TempleCBE`'s joint modeling capabilities across three interconnected layers:

1. **Survival & Counting-Process Audit in `get_dataset_info.R` (`proc_contents`)**: Upgrading `get_dataset_info()` to properly parse counting-process intervals `Surv(tstart, tstop, status)`, leverage `extract_surv_components()` from `R/joint_model.R`, and add S3 dispatch for `joint_model` objects.
2. **Vignette Harmonization**: Introducing `joint_model()` and cross-validating with SAS joint modeling into `vignettes/R_to_SAS.Rmd` and `vignettes/sas_survival.Rmd`.
3. **Alignment with Established JSS Literature**:
   - **Rizopoulos (2010)**, *Journal of Statistical Software* 35(9) (`tasks/to_do/R_SAS_IO_EXAMPLE/v35i09.R`): R `JM` package, distinguishing repeated-measures longitudinal biomarkers (`aids`) from subject-level endpoints (`aids.id`), and contrasting naive time-dependent Cox regression with joint likelihood modeling.
   - **Garcia-Hernandez & Rizopoulos (2018)**, *Journal of Statistical Software* 84(12) (`v84i12.pdf`): SAS `%JM` macro, uniting generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs via `PROC NLMIXED` with adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature) with proportional hazards survival models.

---

# Audit of Current State

## Vignette Audit (Confirmation)

An exhaustive search across all vignette files confirms:
- **`vignettes/R_to_SAS.Rmd`**: Contains data I/O, `%cpdata`, `%coxtvc`, clustered sandwich variance (`cgd`), and macro registration. **`joint_model` is NOT currently present.**
- **`vignettes/sas_survival.Rmd`**: Contains univariable/multivariable Cox models, SAS Example 85.7 start/stop counting-process data, `tmerge`, and `%cbe_brier_score` calibration. **`joint_model` is NOT currently present.**
- **Other Vignettes** (`nested_survival_cv.Rmd`, `reticulate_export.Rmd`, `eda_and_missingness.Rmd`, `compute_graph.Rmd`): Do not contain `joint_model`.

**Conclusion**: `joint_model.R` is currently confined to `R/joint_model.R` and `tests/testthat/test-joint_model.R`. It has not yet been documented or showcased in any vignette.

## Current Limitations in `R/get_dataset_info.R`

In `R/get_dataset_info.R` (lines 85–100):
```r
surv_summary <- function(col) {
  m <- unclass(df[[col]])
  cn <- colnames(m)
  time_idx <- if (!is.null(cn) && "time" %in% cn) which(cn == "time") else 1L
  status_idx <- if (!is.null(cn) && "status" %in% cn) which(cn == "status") else ncol(m)
  time <- m[, time_idx]
  status <- m[, status_idx]
  ...
}
```

### Critical Flaw on Counting-Process Data
When `df[[col]]` is a counting-process survival object `Surv(start, stop, status)`:
- `colnames(m)` are `"start"`, `"stop"`, `"status"`.
- Because `"time"` does not exist in `cn`, `time_idx` defaults to `1L` (`start`, which is entry time, often 0).
- Consequently, `mean(time)` computes the mean entry time rather than elapsed duration (`stop - start`) or terminal follow-up (`stop`).
- In contrast, `R/joint_model.R` contains `extract_surv_components()`, which parses `attr(surv_col, "type")`, distinguishes `"counting"` from `"right"`, and correctly extracts `start`, `stop`, and `status`.

# Technical Specification: Updating `R/get_dataset_info.R`

## Core Enhancements

1. **Direct Integration with `extract_surv_components()`**:
   Decompose `Surv` columns using the formal survival type attribute:
   - **Right-censored (`type == "right"`)**: Mean/SD of follow-up time, event count, and event percentage.
   - **Counting-process (`type == "counting"`)**: Mean/SD of interval duration (`stop - start`), median terminal stop time, total intervals, and distinct subjects.
2. **S3 Method Dispatch**:
   - `get_dataset_info.data.frame(x, subject_id = NULL, ...)`: Base data frame method.
   - `get_dataset_info.joint_model(x, ...)`: Summarizes the joint model's extracted predictor space (`x$components$predictors`), outcome components, sample size, event counts, and sub-model performance metrics.
3. **Longitudinal and Time-Varying Covariate Audit (`subject_id`)**:
   - For longitudinal datasets (such as `aids` in `v35i09.R`), specifying `subject_id = "patient"` enables `get_dataset_info()` to automatically classify every predictor:
     - **Baseline / Time-Invariant**: Exactly 1 unique value per subject (e.g., `drug`, `gender`).
     - **Longitudinal / Time-Varying**: More than 1 unique value per subject (e.g., repeated CD4 counts).
   - Validates interval integrity for start/stop tables: checks that $t_{\text{stop}} > t_{\text{start}}$ for all observations.

## Drop-In Implementation Blueprint

```r
#' Summarize a Data Frame or Joint Model's Columns and Components
#'
#' Per-column metadata: class, variable label (if set via \pkg{labelled}),
#' mean/sd for numeric columns, most-frequent value, distinct-value count,
#' missingness, and survival structure. When provided a \code{\link[TempleCBE]{joint_model}}
#' object, summarizes the fitted training data and sub-model components.
#'
#' @param x A data frame, tibble, or a fitted \code{joint_model} object.
#' @param subject_id Optional character string specifying subject identifier for
#'   longitudinal repeated-measures datasets.
#' @param ... Additional arguments.
#'
#' @return A tibble with per-column metadata and diagnostic attributes.
#' @export
get_dataset_info <- function(x, ...) {
  UseMethod("get_dataset_info")
}

#' @rdname get_dataset_info
#' @export
get_dataset_info.data.frame <- function(x, subject_id = NULL, ...) {
  df <- x
  dataset_name <- deparse(substitute(x))
  columns <- colnames(df)

  is_surv <- vapply(df, function(col) inherits(col, "Surv"), logical(1))
  surv_cols <- columns[is_surv]
  numeric_cols <- setdiff(names(dplyr::select(df, dplyr::where(is.numeric))), surv_cols)

  class_vec <- unname(vapply(columns, function(col) {
    trimws(sub("labelled", "", paste0(class(df[[col]]), collapse = "")))
  }, character(1)))

  # Labels via labelled::var_label with attribute fallback
  var_labels <- tryCatch(labelled::var_label(df), error = function(e) list())
  label_for <- function(col) {
    lbl <- var_labels[[col]]
    if (is.null(lbl) || length(lbl) != 1 || is.na(lbl) || !nzchar(lbl)) {
      lbl <- attr(df[[col]], "label", exact = TRUE)
    }
    if (is.null(lbl) || length(lbl) != 1 || is.na(lbl) || !nzchar(as.character(lbl))) {
      col
    } else {
      as.character(lbl)
    }
  }
  labels_tbl <- tibble::tibble(columns = columns, labels = unname(vapply(columns, label_for, character(1))))

  # Missingness
  na_info <- if (ncol(df) > 0) {
    dplyr::summarise(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), \(v) SumNa(v))) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "columns", values_to = "SumNa") |>
      dplyr::mutate(PctNa = .data$SumNa / nrow(df))
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(columns = character(), SumNa = numeric(), PctNa = numeric())
  }

  # Distinct values
  n_distinct_cols <- setdiff(columns, surv_cols)
  n_distinct <- if (length(n_distinct_cols) > 0) {
    dplyr::summarise(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(n_distinct_cols), \(v) tryCatch(dplyr::n_distinct(v), error = \(e) NA))) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "columns", values_to = "n_distinct")
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(columns = character(), n_distinct = numeric())
  }
  if (length(surv_cols) > 0) {
    surv_n_distinct <- unname(vapply(surv_cols, function(col) {
      tryCatch(nrow(unique(unclass(df[[col]]))), error = \(e) NA_integer_)
    }, numeric(1)))
    n_distinct <- dplyr::bind_rows(n_distinct, tibble::tibble(columns = surv_cols, n_distinct = surv_n_distinct))
  }

  # Numeric summaries
  if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) {
    long <- df |>
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(numeric_cols), as.numeric)) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(numeric_cols), names_to = "columns", values_to = "value_") |>
      dplyr::group_by(.data$columns)
    mean_tbl <- dplyr::summarise(long, mean = mean(.data$value_, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    sd_tbl <- dplyr::summarise(long, sd = stats::sd(.data$value_, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  } else {
    mean_tbl <- tibble::tibble(columns = character(), mean = numeric())
    sd_tbl <- tibble::tibble(columns = character(), sd = numeric())
  }

  # Robust Surv handling using extract_surv_components logic
  surv_summary <- function(col) {
    s_obj <- df[[col]]
    s_type <- attr(s_obj, "type") %||% "right"
    m <- unclass(s_obj)

    if (identical(s_type, "counting")) {
      start_t <- m[, "start"]
      stop_t  <- m[, "stop"]
      status  <- m[, "status"]
      duration <- stop_t - start_t
      n_events <- sum(status == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
      pct_events <- if (length(status) > 0) round(100 * n_events / length(status), 1) else NA_real_

      tibble::tibble(
        columns = col,
        mean = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = stats::sd(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
        most_freq = paste0("Counting (Events: ", n_events, " [", pct_events, "%], Median Follow-up: ",
                           round(stats::median(stop_t, na.rm = TRUE), 1), ")")
      )
    } else {
      time_val <- m[, 1L]
      status_val <- m[, ncol(m)]
      n_events <- sum(status_val == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
      pct_events <- if (length(status_val) > 0) round(100 * n_events / length(status_val), 1) else NA_real_

      tibble::tibble(
        columns = col,
        mean = mean(time_val, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = stats::sd(time_val, na.rm = TRUE),
        most_freq = paste0("Events: ", n_events, " (", pct_events, "%)")
      )
    }
  }

  surv_tbl <- if (length(surv_cols) > 0) {
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(surv_cols, surv_summary))
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(columns = character(), mean = numeric(), sd = numeric(), most_freq = character())
  }
  mean_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(mean_tbl, dplyr::select(surv_tbl, "columns", "mean"))
  sd_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(sd_tbl, dplyr::select(surv_tbl, "columns", "sd"))

  # Most frequent categorical values
  most_freq_val <- function(v) {
    tab <- table(v)
    if (length(tab) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    names(which.max(tab))
  }
  mf_cols <- setdiff(names(dplyr::select(df, dplyr::where(is.factor) | dplyr::where(is.character) |
                                          dplyr::where(is.logical) | dplyr::where(is.numeric))), surv_cols)
  most_freq <- if (length(mf_cols) > 0) {
    dplyr::summarise(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(mf_cols), most_freq_val)) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "columns", values_to = "most_freq")
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(columns = character(), most_freq = character())
  }
  most_freq <- dplyr::bind_rows(most_freq, dplyr::select(surv_tbl, "columns", "most_freq"))

  out <- tibble::tibble(columns = columns, class = class_vec) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dataset_name = dataset_name) |>
    dplyr::left_join(labels_tbl, by = "columns") |>
    dplyr::relocate("labels") |>
    dplyr::relocate("dataset_name") |>
    dplyr::left_join(mean_tbl, by = "columns") |>
    dplyr::left_join(sd_tbl, by = "columns") |>
    dplyr::left_join(most_freq, by = "columns") |>
    dplyr::left_join(n_distinct, by = "columns") |>
    dplyr::left_join(na_info, by = "columns")

  # Optional longitudinal auditing
  if (!is.null(subject_id) && subject_id %in% columns) {
    var_types <- vapply(columns, function(col) {
      if (col == subject_id) return("Subject ID")
      varies <- any(tapply(df[[col]], df[[subject_id]], function(vals) length(unique(vals[!is.na(vals)])) > 1L))
      if (isTRUE(varies)) "Longitudinal (Time-Varying)" else "Baseline (Time-Invariant)"
    }, character(1))
    out <- dplyr::mutate(out, variable_type = var_types)
  }

  out
}

#' @rdname get_dataset_info
#' @export
get_dataset_info.joint_model <- function(x, ...) {
  comp <- x$components
  df <- comp$predictors
  df[[deparse(comp$formula[[2L]])]] <- comp$surv_obj

  res <- get_dataset_info.data.frame(df, ...)
  attr(res, "joint_model_summary") <- list(
    engine = x$engine,
    calibration = x$calibration,
    n_obs = length(comp$time),
    n_events = sum(comp$status),
    event_pct = round(100 * mean(comp$status), 1),
    median_followup = stats::median(comp$time)
  )
  res
}

#' @rdname get_dataset_info
#' @export
proc_contents <- get_dataset_info
```

# Vignette Integration Blueprint

## 1. Integration into `vignettes/R_to_SAS.Rmd`

Add a dedicated section: **"Part 5: Joint Modeling of Longitudinal and Survival Processes (R `joint_model` vs. SAS `%JM` Macro)"**.

### Outline of Content:
- **Theoretical Context**: Introduce the bias of naive time-dependent Cox regression (`coxph` with step-function covariates) when covariates are measured with error or subject to informative dropout.
- **R Implementation**:
  - Audit input datasets using `proc_contents(df, subject_id = "patient")`.
  - Fit `fit <- joint_model(data, Surv(start, stop, status) ~ ., engine = "glmnet")`.
  - Inspect predictions (`predict(fit)` returning `.pred_survival`, `.pred_status_calibrated`, `.pred_time`).
- **SAS Parity via `%JM` Macro** (Garcia-Hernandez & Rizopoulos 2018, *JSS* 84(12)):
  - Show SAS macro syntax for `%JM` with `PROC NLMIXED`:
    ```sas
    %JM(data = aids,
        id = patient,
        time = obstime,
        y = CD4,
        survdata = aids_id,
        survtime = Time,
        status = death,
        model = normal,
        hazard = piecewise);
    ```
  - Cross-compare how R and SAS represent random-effects slopes and joint likelihood estimation.

## 2. Integration into `vignettes/sas_survival.Rmd`

- Update the **SAS to TempleCBE Translation Reference Table** to include:
  | Modeling Paradigm | SAS Implementation | TempleCBE R Implementation |
  |:---|:---|:---|
  | Joint Model (Longitudinal + Survival) | `%JM` macro (`PROC NLMIXED`) | `TempleCBE::joint_model()` |
  | Cross-Validated Joint Assessment | Custom macro loop | `TempleCBE::cv_joint_model()` |
  | Dataset Pre-flight Auditing | `PROC CONTENTS` / `%cpdata` | `get_dataset_info()` / `proc_contents()` |

3. **Step 3**: Add test coverage to `tests/testthat/test-get_dataset_info.R` verifying counting-process `Surv` objects, `joint_model` input, and `subject_id` classification.
